Notes: Chicago uses its own Chicago Construction Codes, not the IRC. Reroofing: 14R-3-306. Roof coverings: 14B-15-1507. Researched Oct 1, 2026 from search results only; code text not opened. Confirm before citing.
Leverage adopted code: Chicago Construction Codes / Existing Building Code
Verified requirement: Roof repair not exceeding 25% of an existing roof may use Chapter 4; roof replacement requires removal of existing roof-covering layers to the deck. Rusted/damaged/deteriorated vent flashing, metal edging, drain outlets, collars and counterflashing may not be reinstalled. Flashings must be reconstructed per manufacturer instructions.
How it helps vs. partial scope: Useful where the carrier scope disturbs/reuses damaged metals or flashing, or where the proposed scope becomes reroofing/replacement. Supports expanded metal/flashing scope and full tear-off once replacement is established.
Carrier argument / limitation: Does NOT say that >25% damage automatically requires full replacement. Use the exact facts and proposed repair method.

Notes: Village site lists the 2003 IRC (may be out of date). 2003 IRC has no drip-edge requirement. Edition is older than the state baseline under PA 103-0510. Local amendments not yet reviewed. Researched Oct 1, 2026.
Verified requirement: Max two layers of 3-tab roofing; architectural shingles cannot be installed over existing shingles; complete tear-off required when existing covering is water-soaked, curling or deteriorated so it is inadequate as a base. Deficient/deteriorated sheathing must be stripped to rafters and re-sheathed. Damaged/rusted/deteriorated vent flashing, metal edging, outlets, collars and counterflashings cannot be reinstalled. Materials must follow code and manufacturer instructions.
How it helps vs. partial scope: Very useful when the carrier proposes overlay/recover, reuse of damaged metals, or a repair over an unsuitable existing roof. Can directly create tear-off and decking/metal scope depending on field conditions.
Carrier argument / limitation: Condition-based. Document the existing layer count, shingle type, deterioration, decking condition and metal condition.
